title: Eventual cohomology stabilization gives stalk injectivity for a derived limit
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, let $(K_n)$ be an inverse system in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, and let $(K,p,\delta)$ be a derived limit of it [def-weil-derived-limit], written $K=R\varprojlim_nK_n$ (any one; derived limits are not unique up to canonical isomorphism). Let $x\in X$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$. Suppose there are an index $n(x)$ and a fundamental system $\mathfrak U_x$ of open neighborhoods of $x$ such that, for every $U\in\mathfrak U_x$, (i) $R^1\varprojlim_n H^{m-1}(U,K_n)=0$, and (ii) for every $n\ge n(x)$ the transition map $H^m(U,K_n)\to H^m(U,K_{n(x)})$ is injective. Then the map on stalks $H^m(K)_x\to H^m(K_{n(x)})_x$ induced by $\mathrm{pr}_{n(x)}\circ p:K\to K_{n(x)}$ is injective. Here cohomology is sheaf cohomology on opens [pqf-def-cohomology].

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-ringed-space-sheafification-cohomology] to obtain P, its sheafification comparison, local representatives and zero detection. For each open U, [lem-pc-cohomology-presheaf-derived-sections-evaluation] naturally identifies P evaluated at U with H^m(RΓ(U,-)).

For every U in the fundamental system, apply the short exact sequence of [lem-pc-ringed-space-rgamma-derived-limit]. Vanishing of its left term makes the right map injective. The inverse-limit projection to level n₀ is injective: for n ≥ n₀ use the assumed injectivity and compatibility, and for n < n₀ apply compatibility to the equal n₀ components. The projection equations identify the composite with H^m(U,p followed by pr_n₀). Transport injectivity to P using naturality of the comparison from [lem-pc-cohomology-presheaf-derived-sections-evaluation].

source.place: Tag 0D61, proof, short exact sequence and hypotheses (1), (2)

proof.text: Represent a stalk element in the kernel by a P-section over U. Naturality on germs makes its image have zero germ, so zero detection gives a smaller neighborhood V where the image vanishes. Choose W in the fundamental system inside V; naturality of restriction still gives zero image. Injectivity on W kills the restricted section. Naturality of the sheafification comparison and invariance of germs under restriction show that the original stalk element is zero.
